parallel.requirements: Parallel recognized the hard requirements, including the b2/argv[6] quirk, f32 arithmetic, no clamping, %g formatting, std::stof grammar, and complete /output project delivery.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It created task cards, then launched a workflow with four recon children before a later implementation owner, fuzzers, reviewers, and gate. The parent simultaneously built a fallback in /tmp.
parallel.implementation: No workflow implementation reached /output. The parent wrote a staged project under /tmp/mine/stage and verified portions of it, but did not copy it into the required deliverable tree.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The required /output artifact was empty at evaluation. The parallel final response was empty, and artifact validation found no test7.rs or executable.
parallel.verification: The parent and children did substantial oracle probing and partial staged checks, but official verification evaluated an empty artifact rather than a promoted implementation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed in the recon phase, the local staging candidate was not finalized into /output, and the official result was 0/39.

serial.requirements: Serial recognized the same byte-exact porting obligations and the non-obvious argv, formatting, parser, and f32 arithmetic constraints.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the full path: probe behavior, write the /output project, compile, fuzz, patch the parser boundary bug, rebuild, and deliver.
serial.implementation: It wrote Cargo.toml, test7.rs, color modules, C++ formatting emulation, and a std::stof-compatible parser directly under /output.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It compiled /output/test7 with rustc and cargo, retained source plus modules in the final tree, and delivered a final response describing the artifact.
serial.verification: It ran unit tests, five documented examples, error-path checks, and 4443 differential fuzz cases before the official evaluator passed all 39 cases.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official residual failure remained; the final response noted only a theoretical hex-float double-rounding limit outside found cases.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is discordant because the serial run produced a complete /output project and passed all 39 tests, while the parallel run timed out with an empty artifact. The concrete process difference is not task comprehension: parallel had strong behavioral facts and even a staged candidate. The difference is that parallel gated workflow implementation behind a broad recon phase and then failed to promote its parent-local staging candidate before timeout; serial wrote directly to /output, fixed a fuzz-found bug, and verified the submitted artifact.
parallel_contributors: A workflow-wide recon barrier awaited all recon children before implementation, and the workflow was killed before any workflow implementation was produced.
The parent's verified staging candidate remained under /tmp/mine/stage instead of being copied into /output before timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one owner for probing through delivery and wrote all required files directly to /output.
Serial reran unit tests, documented examples, and 4443 differential fuzz cases against the final artifact before closing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial found and fixed an ordinary strtof tininess-boundary bug before closure; parallel had no residual submitted implementation to compare.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned an implementation agent to own /output, and the parent also built a local staging implementation; the problem was gating and finalization, not absence of an implementer.
No multiple independently completed component implementations needed reconciliation; the final artifact was absent rather than incompatible.
The workflow implementation prompt owned the package layout and deliverable placement, and the parent had a local staged package; late promotion, not owner absence, is the evidenced issue.
The workflow script defined an end-to-end recon, implement, fuzz, review, and gate pipeline; it failed to progress through that pipeline before timeout.
The gate was not one mandatory preflight or oracle harness; it was a multi-lens investigation phase before implementation.

The parallel workflow awaited all recon children before phase('Implement') and never reached the implementation owner after a recon child stalled/retried. The serial run moved from behavior mapping to writing /output directly.
candidates.realized_consequence: The workflow implementation phase never produced any /output files, leaving the official artifact empty.
candidates.near_match_reason: The strtof recon child was broad and stalled, but retaining it as load imbalance would duplicate the same recon-barrier episode; the actionable boundary is implementation being deferred behind the complete investigation phase.

candidates.reason: The critical implementation path was gated by the recon phase, not merely underallocated while auxiliary workers consumed capacity.
The evidence shows four recon children plus a retry, not excessive breadth as the primary boundary; the same budget loss is already captured by Serial Investigation.
The strtof child had a broad scope and stalled, but that stall is part of the retained recon-barrier chain and does not get a separate load-imbalance label.
The executed recon child briefs carried detailed task facts and requested specific acceptance evidence; no already-known required fact is shown missing from a child brief and causing unusable work.
No independently owned components were integrated under incompatible filenames, exports, or contracts; the implementation owner never received all recon inputs.
The record does not show a known finding disappearing through transfer and causing repeated work; missing returns are due to unfinished recon, not lossy summarization.
Completed handoffs were long, but there is no decision point where an available bulky result was too large to consume; the workflow was killed before aggregation and implementation.
No receiver is shown consuming a superseded workspace, dependency, or requirement state; the problem is unstarted implementation and unpromoted staging.
No incompatible returned contracts or reports reached a parent decision point and remained unadjudicated.
Parallel made no observable whole-task completion claim; its final response is empty and status shows timeout, so this is absence of finalization rather than unsupported acceptance.

A strtof retry occurred after a stall, but the retained consequence is the recon barrier preventing implementation; there is insufficient separate evidence that lack of checkpoint inheritance independently caused repeated failed output.

candidates.reason: No child implementation was merged after integrated verification, and the parent-local staging candidate was never merged into /output at all.
No delegated implementation child completed a retrievable result; the unpromoted candidate was produced locally by the parent under /tmp, so Late Finalization is the closer label.
The workflow never reached verifier children, so no concrete verifier finding was trapped below the parent.
The parent did take over substantial work by building a staged implementation locally; the remaining adverse episode is failure to promote it before timeout.
Completed recon results were not ignored in favor of an inconsistent final decision; the workflow was waiting for missing recon and the parent separately worked locally.
The parent repeatedly checked workflow progress and continued local staging and fuzz work, so the timeout was not a blind wait without inspection.
No concurrent agents produced competing final-tree implementations or overlapping interfaces that required reconciliation.
There is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source or configuration file and observing or reconciling concurrent changes.
No non-entry source file produced by one actor was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another actor.
The deliverable was absent, not overwritten; no actor replaced /output/test7.rs or the submitted executable while another owned it.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced another actor's final workspace outputs.
Although several actors wrote scratch files, no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from shared implementation workspace writes is shown.
No generated scratch artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as stable input in a contaminating way.

retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The strtof recon child was broad and stalled, but that is the same stalled-child chain as the recon barrier and is not retained separately.
